text: Rahu Kaal is one eighth of the daytime, chosen by the weekday (Monday 2nd, Saturday 3rd, Friday 4th, Wednesday 5th, Thursday 6th, Tuesday 7th, Sunday 8th part); new beginnings are avoided in it.
Yamaganda is one eighth of the daytime fixed by the weekday (Sunday 5th, Monday 4th, Tuesday 3rd, Wednesday 2nd, Thursday 1st, Friday 7th, Saturday 6th part) and is left out when choosing a time.

Gulika (Mandi) is Saturn's eighth of the daytime, counted from the weekday lord (Sunday 7th, Monday 6th, Tuesday 5th, Wednesday 4th, Thursday 3rd, Friday 2nd, Saturday 1st part), and is avoided for starting work.
Abhijit is the 8th of the 15 daytime muhurtas, the 48 minutes centred on local noon, and is counted as favourable on every weekday in this app (some almanacs omit Wednesdays).
Brahma muhurta is the second-last muhurta of the night, from 96 to 48 minutes before the next sunrise, kept for study and quiet practice.
Amrit choghadiya is the Moon's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as favourable.
Shubh choghadiya is Jupiter's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as favourable.
Labh choghadiya is Mercury's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as favourable.
Chal choghadiya is Venus's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and counts as neutral.
Rog choghadiya is Mars's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and is avoided for starting work.
Kaal choghadiya is Saturn's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and is avoided for starting work.
Udveg choghadiya is the Sun's eighth of the day or night in the weekday sequence and is avoided for starting work.
Each hora is one twelfth of the day or of the night, ruled in turn by Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter and Mars starting from the weekday lord at sunrise.

Bhadra is the Vishti karana, the first half of Shukla 8 and 15 and Krishna 7 and 14 and the second half of Shukla 4 and 11 and Krishna 3 and 10; it matters on earth only when the Moon is in Mesha, Vrishabha, Mithuna or Vrishchika, and new beginnings are then deferred.

Panchak runs while the Moon travels the last 300 to 360 degrees of the zodiac (Dhanishtha second half to Revati), when five kinds of work, such as roofing, bedding, travel south and cremation, are traditionally not begun.
Disha Shool names one direction per weekday in which a journey is not begun: east on Monday and Saturday, north on Tuesday and Wednesday, south on Thursday, west on Sunday and Friday.
Chandra bala counts the house of today's Moon from your birth Moon: the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th and 11th are favourable, the others are not, and the 8th is Chandrashtama.
The Moon returns to your birth sign today (1st from the natal Moon), a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 2nd sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 3rd sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 4th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 5th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 6th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 7th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 8th sign from your birth Moon today (Chandrashtama), the house Chandra bala sets aside; routine work continues, new starts wait for the Moon to move on.
The Moon is in the 9th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
The Moon is in the 10th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 11th sign from your birth Moon today, a favourable house in Chandra bala.
The Moon is in the 12th sign from your birth Moon today, which Chandra bala does not count as favourable.
Chandrashtama is the roughly two and a quarter days each month when the transiting Moon is in the 8th sign from your birth Moon; it is a day for routine, not for launches.

Tara bala counts from your birth nakshatra to today's nakshatra in cycles of nine: Sampat (2), Kshema (4), Sadhaka (6), Mitra (8) and Parama Mitra (9) are favourable; Janma (1), Vipat (3), Pratyari (5) and Vadha (7, also called Naidhana) are not.
Today's nakshatra is your Janma tara (1st of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is treated as neutral to unfavourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Sampat tara (2nd of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Vipat tara (3rd of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is not favourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Kshema tara (4th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Pratyari tara (5th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is not favourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Sadhaka tara (6th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Vadha tara (7th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is not favourable for new starts.
Today's nakshatra is your Mitra tara (8th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
Today's nakshatra is your Parama Mitra tara (9th of nine), counted from your birth nakshatra; it is favourable.
The day's tithi, nakshatra, yoga and weekday are read together from the Moon and Sun at sunrise, with Bhadra and Panchak noted as flags; special yogas arise from fixed weekday and nakshatra pairs.
Sade Sati is Saturn's transit through the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from your birth Moon, about seven and a half years in three phases; Dhaiya is Saturn's two and a half years in the 4th or 8th sign.
Phase 1 of Sade Sati: Saturn is in the 12th sign from your birth Moon, the opening two and a half years of the transit.
Phase 2 of Sade Sati: Saturn is in the same sign as your birth Moon, the middle two and a half years of the transit.
Phase 3 of Sade Sati: Saturn is in the 2nd sign from your birth Moon, the closing two and a half years of the transit.
Saturn is currently neither in the 12th, 1st, 2nd, 4th nor 8th sign from your birth Moon, so no Sade Sati or Dhaiya applies; the next one starts when Saturn enters such a sign.
Kantaka Dhaiya: Saturn is in the 4th sign from your birth Moon for about two and a half years.
Ashtama Dhaiya: Saturn is in the 8th sign from your birth Moon for about two and a half years.
The running Vimshottari mahadasha and antardasha lords are compared with today's weekday lord by Parashara's natural friendships, and their horas of the day are listed.
For each family member the same Chandra bala (Moon house from the birth Moon) and Tara bala (nakshatra count from the birth nakshatra) are computed from their own chart.
A planet is exalted (uchcha) in one fixed sign: Sun in Mesha, Moon in Vrishabha, Mars in Makara, Mercury in Kanya, Jupiter in Karka, Venus in Meena, Saturn in Tula.
A planet is debilitated (neecha) in the sign opposite its exaltation: Sun in Tula, Moon in Vrishchika, Mars in Karka, Mercury in Meena, Jupiter in Makara, Venus in Kanya, Saturn in Mesha.
A planet is in its own sign (swakshetra) when it rules the sign it occupies; moolatrikona is folded into this tag.
A planet is in a friend's sign when the sign's lord is its natural friend in Parashara's table of friendships.
A planet is in an enemy's sign when the sign's lord is its natural enemy in Parashara's table of friendships.
A planet is in a neutral sign when the sign's lord is neither friend nor enemy in Parashara's table of friendships.
A planet is combust (asta) when it lies within its orb of the Sun: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° retrograde), Saturn 15°.
A planet is retrograde (vakri) when its longitude decreases from day to day as seen from Earth; the Sun and Moon never are, Rahu and Ketu almost always are.
A planet is vargottama when it occupies the same sign in the D1 Rashi chart and the D9 Navamsa.
Vargottama means the D1 and D9 signs coincide, which happens in the first navamsa of a movable sign, the fifth of a fixed sign and the ninth of a dual sign.
Combustion orbs used: Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14° (12° when retrograde), Jupiter 11°, Venus 10° (8° when retrograde), Saturn 15°; Rahu and Ketu are never combust.
This value carries approx. because the birth time was entered as approximate and shifting it by the stated minutes would move the value across a sign or house boundary.
This value carries approx. because the body lies within 1° of a sign boundary, where small differences in ayanamsa or time would change its sign.
With the birth time unknown the Lagna cannot be computed, so the Moon sign is placed in house 1 and houses are counted from it; dashas stay valid because they depend only on the Moon.
The Lagna is the sidereal sign rising on the eastern horizon at the birth time and place; it moves one sign roughly every two hours, so the chart is only as exact as the recorded time.

In whole-sign houses each house is one full sign counted from the Lagna, and its lord is the ruler of that sign: Mars (Mesha, Vrishchika), Venus (Vrishabha, Tula), Mercury (Mithuna, Kanya), Moon (Karka), Sun (Simha), Jupiter (Dhanu, Meena), Saturn (Makara, Kumbha).

Vimshottari dasha runs 120 years in the order Ketu 7, Venus 20, Sun 6, Moon 10, Mars 7, Rahu 18, Jupiter 16, Saturn 19, Mercury 17, starting from the lord of the birth nakshatra with a balance proportional to how much of it the Moon had still to cross.
A dasha change is the exact instant a maha, antar or pratyantar period ends, computed with a dasha year of 365.2425 days from the birth moment.
The janma tithi is the lunar month, paksha and tithi at the moment of birth; its anniversary is the day on which that tithi prevails at sunrise (udaya), skipping an Adhik month.
The barsi is the yearly shraddha on the tithi of passing, taken on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna); the same tithi number gives the Pitru Paksha day.
Pitru Paksha is the dark fortnight of Bhadrapada (Purnimanta Ashwin), from Purnima shraddha to Sarva Pitru Amavasya, each day matched to a tithi by the afternoon (aparahna) rule.
When the lunar month repeats as an Adhik month, recurring observances fall in the nija (regular) month of the same name, not in the Adhik one.
When a tithi begins after one sunrise and ends before the next (kshaya), it touches no sunrise, so the observance is kept on the day it begins.
Saturn's sign entry is the exact moment its sidereal longitude crosses a sign boundary, found by search, including retrograde re-entries.
Jupiter's sign entry is the exact moment its sidereal longitude crosses a sign boundary, found by search, including retrograde re-entries.
Rahu's sign entry is the moment the lunar node's sidereal longitude (mean node by default) crosses a sign boundary moving backwards; Ketu enters the opposite sign at the same time.

Ekadashi is kept on the day whose sunrise has the eleventh tithi (Smarta), or on the next day for Vaishnavas when Dashami still runs at dawn; parana follows the end of Hari Vasara within the Dwadashi, before a fifth of the day has passed.
Pradosh is the day the thirteenth tithi prevails at pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night after sunset, and is named by its weekday (Soma, Bhauma, Shani Pradosh).
Sankashti Chaturthi is the Krishna fourth tithi on the day it covers moonrise; on a Tuesday it is Angaraki.
Vinayaka Chaturthi is the Shukla fourth tithi on the day it covers midday (madhyahna).
Masik Shivaratri is the Krishna fourteenth tithi on the night it covers midnight (nishita).
The Purnima vrat is kept on the day the full-moon tithi prevails at moonrise, when the fast is broken.
Amavasya observances are kept on the day the new-moon tithi prevails at sunrise.
Karwa Chauth is Kartik Krishna Chaturthi on the day it covers moonrise; the fast runs from sunrise to that moonrise.
Chhath is Kartik Shukla Shashthi at sunrise, with Nahay Khay on Chaturthi, Kharna on Panchami, the evening arghya at sunset on Shashthi and the morning arghya at the next sunrise.
Hariyali Teej is Shravana Shukla Tritiya, Kajari Teej Bhadrapada Krishna Tritiya and Hartalika Teej Bhadrapada Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta names), each on the day whose sunrise has the tithi.
Navratri runs the nine days from Pratipada in Chaitra or Ashwin Shukla paksha; Ghatasthapana is done in the Pratipada while it runs after sunrise, or in Abhijit when it ends early.
The Satyanarayan vrat is kept on the Purnima day whose evening (sunset) still has the full-moon tithi, otherwise on the day it is at sunrise.
Makar Sankranti is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Makara (Makara sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Pongal (Thai Pongal) (observed in the south) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Makara (Makara sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Lohri (observed in the north) is 1 day before Makar Sankranti.
Thaipusam (observed in the south) is the day in the solar month of Makara whose sunrise has Pushya nakshatra; when two days qualify, the one with more daylight under that nakshatra is taken.
Vasant Panchami (Saraswati Puja) falls on Magha Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the forenoon (purvahna).
Ratha Saptami falls on Magha Shukla Saptami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Bhishma Ashtami falls on Magha Shukla Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), taking the day on which the tithi covers more of that period when it touches it on two days.

Jaya Ekadashi falls on Magha Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Magha Purnima falls on Magha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Mauni Amavasya falls on Magha Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Shattila Ekadashi falls on Magha Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Vijaya Ekadashi falls on Phalguna Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Amalaki Ekadashi falls on Phalguna Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Holika Dahan falls on Phalguna Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days, and the observance moves past any Bhadra (Vishti karana) that overlaps the window.
Holi (Dhulandi) is 1 day after Holika Dahan.
Rang Panchami (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Krishna Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Sheetala Ashtami (Basoda) (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Papmochani Ekadashi falls on Chaitra Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Ugadi (Telugu/Kannada New Year) (observed in the south) falls on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Gudi Padwa (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Chaitra Navratri runs from Chaitra Shukla Pratipada to Navami (Purnimanta month name), each day taken by the tithi at sunrise, so the span can be eight or ten days when a tithi is lost or repeated.
Gangaur (Gauri Tritiya) (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Rama Navami falls on Chaitra Shukla Navami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), taking the day on which the tithi covers more of that period when it touches it on two days.

Kamada Ekadashi falls on Chaitra Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Mahavir Jayanti falls on Chaitra Shukla Trayodashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Hanuman Jayanti (observed in the north) falls on Chaitra Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Hanuman Jayanti (Tamil, Margazhi Amavasya) (observed in the south) falls on Pausha Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Chaitra Purnima falls on Chaitra Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Baisakhi (observed in the north) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Mesha (Mesha sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Vishu (observed in the south) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Mesha (Mesha sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Puthandu (Tamil New Year) (observed in the south) is the day of the Sun's entry into sidereal Mesha (Mesha sankranti), or the following day when the sankranti happens after sunset.
Akshaya Tritiya falls on Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, provided it runs at least 3 muhurtas after that sunrise (else the day before).
Parashurama Jayanti falls on Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).

Ganga Saptami (observed in the north) falls on Vaishakha Shukla Saptami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers midday (madhyahna), taking the day on which the tithi covers more of that period when it touches it on two days.

Buddha Purnima falls on Vaishakha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Vat Savitri Vrat (observed in the north) falls on Jyeshtha Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Vat Purnima Vrat (observed in the south) falls on Jyeshtha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).
Ganga Dussehra (observed in the north) falls on Jyeshtha Shukla Dashami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Varalakshmi Vratam (observed in the south) is the last Friday before Shravana Shukla Purnima.

Raksha Bandhan falls on Shravana Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna), and the observance moves past any Bhadra (Vishti karana) that overlaps the window.
Kajari Teej (observed in the north) falls on Bhadrapada Krishna Tritiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Hal Shashthi (Lalahi Chhath) (observed in the north) falls on Bhadrapada Krishna Shashthi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Onam (Thiruvonam) (observed in the south) is the day in the solar month of Simha whose sunrise has Shravana nakshatra; when two days qualify, the one with more daylight under that nakshatra is taken.

Pitru Paksha begins (Purnima Shraddha) is the Purnima shraddha that opens the dark fortnight of Bhadrapada (Purnimanta Ashwin); each following day is matched to a tithi by the afternoon (aparahna) rule down to Sarva Pitru Amavasya.
Jivitputrika (Jitiya) (observed in the north) falls on Ashwin Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Sharad Navratri runs from Ashwin Shukla Pratipada to Navami (Purnimanta month name), each day taken by the tithi at sunrise, so the span can be eight or ten days when a tithi is lost or repeated.

Maha Navami is 1 day before Dussehra (Vijaya Dashami).
Dussehra (Vijaya Dashami) falls on Ashwin Shukla Dashami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna).

Papankusha Ekadashi falls on Ashwin Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Sharad Purnima (Kojagari) falls on Ashwin Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the night that tithi covers midnight (nishita).
Karwa Chauth (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Krishna Chaturthi (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers moonrise.
Ahoi Ashtami (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).

Rama Ekadashi falls on Kartik Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Dhanteras falls on Kartik Krishna Trayodashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.
Naraka Chaturdashi (Kali Chaudas) falls on Kartik Krishna Chaturdashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Diwali (Lakshmi Puja) falls on Kartik Krishna Amavasya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.
Govardhan Puja (Annakut) falls on Kartik Shukla Pratipada (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Bhai Dooj falls on Kartik Shukla Dwitiya (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the afternoon (aparahna), preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days.
Labh Panchami (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Chhath Puja (observed in the north) falls on Kartik Shukla Shashthi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Skanda Shashthi (Soorasamharam) (observed in the south) falls on Kartik Shukla Shashthi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Gopashtami falls on Kartik Shukla Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Akshaya Navami (Amla Navami) falls on Kartik Shukla Navami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Dev Uthani Ekadashi (Prabodhini) falls on Kartik Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Tulsi Vivah falls on Kartik Shukla Dwadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.
Kartik Purnima (Dev Deepawali) falls on Kartik Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Karthigai Deepam (observed in the south) is the day in the solar month of Vrishchika whose sunset falls in Krittika nakshatra (the lamps are lit at dusk); when no sunset falls in it, the day with more daylight under that nakshatra is taken.
Kalabhairav Jayanti falls on Margashirsha Krishna Ashtami (Purnimanta month name), on the night that tithi covers midnight (nishita).

Utpanna Ekadashi falls on Margashirsha Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Vivah Panchami falls on Margashirsha Shukla Panchami (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

Gita Jayanti (Mokshada Ekadashi) falls on Margashirsha Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Dattatreya Jayanti falls on Margashirsha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day that tithi covers the evening (pradosh kala, the first tenth of the night).

Saphala Ekadashi falls on Pausha Krishna Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.

Pausha Putrada Ekadashi falls on Pausha Shukla Ekadashi (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi, preferring the later day when the tithi covers that time on two days; when the following Dwadashi touches no sunrise, the fast stays on the day the Ekadashi began so that the parana falls inside the Dwadashi.
Pausha Purnima falls on Pausha Shukla Purnima (Purnimanta month name), on the day whose sunrise has that tithi.

D2 Hora (Parashara) splits each sign in two: in odd signs the first 15° belong to the Sun's hora (Simha) and the second 15° to the Moon's hora (Karka), in even signs the reverse, and the chart is read for wealth and provision.
D3 Drekkana divides each sign into three parts of 10°, placed in the sign itself, the 5th sign and the 9th sign from it, and is read for siblings, courage and effort.
D4 Chaturthamsa divides each sign into four parts of 7°30′, placed in the sign itself, the 4th, the 7th and the 10th sign from it, and is read for home, land and fixed property.
D7 Saptamsa divides each sign into seven parts counted from the sign itself in odd signs and from the 7th sign in even signs, and is read for children and what one brings forth.
D9 Navamsa divides the zodiac into 108 equal parts of 3°20′ counted from Mesha, so each sign holds nine navamsas, and is read for partnership, the strength behind the D1 placements and vargottama.
D10 Dasamsa divides each sign into ten parts of 3° counted from the sign itself in odd signs and from the 9th sign in even signs, and is read for work, standing and public duty.
D12 Dwadasamsa divides each sign into twelve parts of 2°30′ counted from the sign itself, and is read for parents and lineage.
D16 Shodasamsa divides each sign into sixteen parts counted from Mesha for movable signs, from Simha for fixed signs and from Dhanu for dual signs, and is read for vehicles, comforts and ease.

D20 Vimsamsa divides each sign into twenty parts counted from Mesha for movable signs, from Dhanu for fixed signs and from Simha for dual signs, and is read for practice, devotion and inner discipline.
D24 Chaturvimsamsa divides each sign into twenty-four parts counted from Simha in odd signs and from Karka in even signs, and is read for learning and study.

D27 Saptavimsamsa (Bhamsa) divides each sign into twenty-seven parts counted from Mesha for fiery signs, Karka for earthy, Tula for airy and Makara for watery signs, and is read for general strength and stamina.

D30 Trimsamsa gives unequal parts to five planets, in odd signs Mars 0–5° (Mesha), Saturn 5–10° (Kumbha), Jupiter 10–18° (Dhanu), Mercury 18–25° (Mithuna) and Venus 25–30° (Tula), in even signs Venus 0–5° (Vrishabha), Mercury 5–12° (Kanya), Jupiter 12–20° (Meena), Saturn 20–25° (Makara) and Mars 25–30° (Vrishchika), and is read for obstacles and how they are met.
D40 Khavedamsa divides each sign into forty parts counted from Mesha in odd signs and from Tula in even signs, and is read for the maternal line and inherited habits.
D45 Akshavedamsa divides each sign into forty-five parts counted from Mesha for movable signs, Simha for fixed signs and Dhanu for dual signs, and is read for character and the paternal line.

D60 Shashtyamsa divides each sign into sixty parts of 30′ counted from the sign itself, and is read for the finest grain of the chart and the carried-over pattern of earlier action (the sixty deity names are not shown in this version).

The Bhinnashtakavarga (BAV) of a planet gives one bindu to every sign that stands in a favourable place counted from each of eight reference points (the seven planets Sun to Saturn and the Lagna), with the favourable places fixed per planet by the classical tables, so the Sun's grid totals 48, the Moon's 49, Mars's 39, Mercury's 54, Jupiter's 56, Venus's 52 and Saturn's 39.
The Sarvashtakavarga (SAV) adds the seven planets' bindus sign by sign, always totalling 337 across the twelve signs, so each house's count can be compared with the average of about 28.
A house is called strong when its Sarvashtakavarga bindus are 28 or more (above the 337/12 average), average at 25 to 27 and weak at 24 or fewer, the usual reading of the SAV totals.

KP house cusps are the twelve Placidus cusps computed in the tropical frame from the birth time and place (Ascendant and Midheaven exact, the intermediate cusps by semi-arc trisection) and then reduced by the KP ayanamsa, so each house runs from its cusp to the next.

Every longitude has a sign lord, a star lord (the nakshatra lord), a sub lord and a sub-sub lord, each sub division splitting its nakshatra in the Vimshottari proportions of 120 and starting with the star's own lord.

The significators of a house are listed in four grades: A, planets in the star of an occupant of the house; B, the occupants; C, planets in the star of the house's cusp lord; D, the cusp lord itself, while Rahu and Ketu act as agents of the planets whose signs they occupy or that join them.

The ruling planets of a moment are the sub lord, star lord and sign lord of the Lagna, the sub lord, star lord and sign lord of the Moon, and the lord of the weekday (Vedic day at the place), listed once each in that order, with a node in the star of a ruling planet added as its agent.
Ruchaka, one of the five Mahapurusha yogas, is formed when Mars stands in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house) in its own sign or its exaltation sign, and is set aside when Mars is combust.
Bhadra yoga, one of the five Mahapurusha yogas, is formed when Mercury stands in a kendra in its own sign or its exaltation sign, and is set aside when Mercury is combust.
Hamsa yoga, one of the five Mahapurusha yogas, is formed when Jupiter stands in a kendra in its own sign or its exaltation sign, and is set aside when Jupiter is combust.
Malavya yoga, one of the five Mahapurusha yogas, is formed when Venus stands in a kendra in its own sign or its exaltation sign, and is set aside when Venus is combust.
Sasa yoga, one of the five Mahapurusha yogas, is formed when Saturn stands in a kendra in its own sign or its exaltation sign, and is set aside when Saturn is combust.
Gaja Kesari yoga is formed when Jupiter stands in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th sign) counted from the Moon, and is set aside when that Jupiter is combust or debilitated.
Budhaditya yoga is formed when the Sun and Mercury occupy the same sign, whichever house that is.
Chandra-Mangala yoga is formed when the Moon and Mars occupy the same sign.
Sunapha yoga is formed when one or more planets other than the Sun, Rahu and Ketu occupy the 2nd sign from the Moon while the 12th from the Moon is empty of them.
Anapha yoga is formed when one or more planets other than the Sun, Rahu and Ketu occupy the 12th sign from the Moon while the 2nd from the Moon is empty of them.
Durudhara yoga is formed when planets other than the Sun, Rahu and Ketu occupy both the 2nd and the 12th sign from the Moon.

Kemadruma is formed when no planet other than the Sun, Rahu and Ketu occupies the 2nd or the 12th sign from the Moon, and it is cancelled when such a planet joins the Moon, stands in a kendra from the Moon or stands in a kendra from the Lagna.
Vesi yoga is formed when one or more planets other than the Moon, Rahu and Ketu occupy the 2nd sign from the Sun while the 12th from the Sun is empty of them.
Vasi yoga is formed when one or more planets other than the Moon, Rahu and Ketu occupy the 12th sign from the Sun while the 2nd from the Sun is empty of them.
Ubhayachari yoga is formed when planets other than the Moon, Rahu and Ketu occupy both the 2nd and the 12th sign from the Sun.
Adhi yoga is formed when the three natural benefics Mercury, Jupiter and Venus all stand in the 6th, 7th or 8th sign counted from the Moon.
Vasumati yoga is formed when the natural benefics Mercury, Jupiter and Venus all stand in upachaya houses (3rd, 6th, 10th or 11th) counted from the Lagna or all from the Moon.
Amala yoga is formed when a natural benefic (Mercury, Jupiter or Venus) stands in the 10th house from the Lagna or in the 10th sign from the Moon.
Saraswati yoga is formed when Jupiter, Venus and Mercury each stand in a kendra, a trikona or the 2nd house and Jupiter is in its own, exaltation or a friend's sign.
Lakshmi yoga is formed when the lord of the 9th house stands in its own or exaltation sign in a kendra or trikona while the Lagna lord is neither debilitated nor combust.
Shakata yoga is formed when Jupiter stands in the 6th, 8th or 12th sign counted from the Moon, and it is cancelled when that Jupiter is in a kendra from the Lagna.
Guru-Chandala yoga is formed when Jupiter shares a sign with Rahu or with Ketu.

Kala Sarpa yoga is formed when all seven planets from the Sun to Saturn lie on one side of the Rahu–Ketu axis with none sharing a node's sign, counted from Rahu towards Ketu for the classical form and from Ketu towards Rahu for the reversed (Kala Amrita) form, and its type takes the number of Rahu's house.

Neecha Bhanga Raja yoga is formed when a debilitated planet has its fall cancelled because the lord of its debilitation sign or the lord of its exaltation sign stands in a kendra from the Lagna or the Moon, because the planet itself stands in such a kendra, or because it exchanges signs with the lord of the sign it occupies.
Harsha, the first Vipreet Raja yoga, is formed when the lord of the 6th house stands in a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th house).
Sarala, the second Vipreet Raja yoga, is formed when the lord of the 8th house stands in a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th house).
Vimala, the third Vipreet Raja yoga, is formed when the lord of the 12th house stands in a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th house).
This Dhana yoga is formed when the lords of the 2nd and the 11th house share a sign, exchange signs or aspect each other by Parashara's full aspects.
A Raja yoga is formed when the lord of a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) and the lord of a trikona (5th or 9th) share a sign or exchange signs, and every such pair in the chart is listed.
Dharma-Karmadhipati yoga is formed when the lords of the 9th and the 10th house share a sign or exchange signs.

Parivartana (exchange) yoga is formed when two planets each occupy the sign the other rules, called Maha when both houses are among 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10 and 11, Khala when one is the 3rd and Dainya when one is a dusthana, and a chart whose exchanges are all Dainya is shown as cancelled.
Kemadruma is cancelled when a planet other than the Moon, Rahu and Ketu stands in the 4th, 7th or 10th sign counted from the Moon.
Kemadruma is cancelled when a planet other than the Moon, Rahu and Ketu stands in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house) from the Lagna.
Kemadruma is cancelled when a planet other than the Sun, Rahu and Ketu shares the Moon's sign.
Gaja Kesari is set aside when the Jupiter forming it is combust or in its debilitation sign, because the yoga asks for a Jupiter with its own strength.
Shakata yoga is cancelled when Jupiter, though in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon, stands in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house) from the Lagna.
A Mahapurusha yoga is set aside when the planet forming it is combust, since a planet too close to the Sun cannot confer the yoga.
A Parivartana whose exchanged houses include the 6th, 8th or 12th is the Dainya kind and is shown as cancelled rather than as a formed yoga.

The Vedic year (varsha pravesha) begins at the instant the sidereal Sun returns to its exact natal longitude in the given calendar year, found by search with the natal chart's ayanamsa, and the annual chart is cast for that instant at the birthplace.

The Muntha is the natal Lagna sign advanced by one sign for every completed year of age, and its house is read in the annual chart (the Moon sign stands in when the birth time is unknown, marked approx.).

The year lord (Varshesha) is chosen among five candidates, the Muntha lord, the natal Lagna lord, the annual Lagna lord, the tri-rashi lord of the annual Lagna and the lord of the Sun's sign for a day return or of the Moon's sign for a night return, keeping only those that aspect the annual Lagna by a Tajika aspect, preferring a friendly aspect, then the highest Panchavargiya bala, with ties going to the day/night lord.

Panchavargiya bala sums five strengths in vishwa, kshetra (sign), uccha (exaltation distance), hadda (terms), drekkana and navamsa, each scaled by the planet's six-fold relationship to the ruler of that division, and the total divided by four grades the planet weak below 5, ordinary from 5 to 10, powerful from 10 to 15 and very strong at 15 or more.

Tajika aspects are read by sign distance, 3rd/11th friendly, 5th/9th secret friendly, 1st/7th inimical and 4th/10th secret inimical, while 2nd/12th and 6th/8th form no aspect (orb-based ithasala is not computed in this version).

The Mudda dasha divides the year from this solar return to the next in the Vimshottari proportions (each planet's years out of 120), starting from the lord of the natal Moon's nakshatra, so the periods add up to exactly one year.
The transit calendar lists the sidereal sign of the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu through the year with the instant each sign change happens, marking entries made while retrograde.
The tithi rule is met when the tithi running for most of the window is in the activity's allowed list (the rikta tithis 4, 9 and 14, Amavasya and the activity's other excluded tithis fail it).
The nakshatra rule is met when the nakshatra running for most of the window is in the activity's allowed list.
The vara rule is met when the weekday of the Vedic day (sunrise to sunrise) is in the activity's allowed list.
The Chandra bala rule is met when the transit Moon stands in the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th or 11th sign from the natal Moon of every profile chosen for the search.
The Tara bala rule is met when the day's nakshatra counted from each profile's birth nakshatra falls on a favourable tara, Sampat (2), Kshema (4), Sadhaka (6), Mitra (8) or Param Mitra (9).
The Rahu Kaal rule is met when the window does not touch the day's Rahu Kaal, which every candidate satisfies because windows are clipped to exclude it before scoring.
The Bhadra rule is met when the window does not overlap a Vishti karana (Bhadra) whose residence is earth, since Bhadra in heaven or the underworld is held harmless.
The Panchak rule is met when the window does not overlap Panchak, the stretch while the Moon moves from the third pada of Dhanishta to the end of Revati.
The Abhijit rule is a bonus met when the window overlaps the Abhijit muhurta, the 48 minutes centred on local noon, and it never creates a window on its own.
The choghadiya rule is met when every choghadiya segment inside the window is Shubh, Labh or Amrit, so a window touching Chal (neutral), Rog, Kaal or Udveg fails it.

Griha pravesh windows follow the Vastu chapter of the Muhurta Chintamani, daytime only, on the allowed tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and their Krishna counterparts, in the fixed and soft nakshatras it names (Ashwini, Rohini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Uttara Bhadrapada, Revati), on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Vehicle purchase windows follow the Vahana chapter, daytime only, avoiding the rikta tithis 4, 9 and 14 together with 8 and Amavasya, in the same soft and fixed nakshatras used for griha pravesh, on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Business start windows follow the Vyapara verses, daytime only, on tithis 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, in the soft and fixed nakshatras, on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Job joining and interview windows follow the Seva verses, daytime only, avoiding tithis 4, 8, 9, 14 and Amavasya, in the soft and fixed nakshatras with Uttara Bhadrapada left out, on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Travel windows follow the Yatra chapter, day or night, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 and their Krishna counterparts, in the nine moving and soft nakshatras it names (Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Anuradha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Revati), on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, with Disha Shool read separately for the direction.

Naamkaran windows follow the Samskara chapter, daytime only, avoiding the rikta tithis 4, 9 and 14 with 8 and Amavasya, in the soft and fixed nakshatras, on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Mundan (Chudakarana) windows follow the Samskara chapter, daytime only, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 and their Krishna counterparts, in the nakshatras it names for the first haircut (Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Jyeshtha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Revati), on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Engagement (roka, vagdana) windows follow the Vivaha chapter, day or night, for two profiles, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, in the marriage nakshatras (Rohini, Mrigashira, Magha, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Swati, Anuradha, Mula, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada, Revati), on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Basic marriage windows follow the Vivaha chapter, day or night, for two profiles, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12 and 13 and their Krishna counterparts, in the eleven marriage nakshatras, on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, without the Lagna-based refinements a pandit adds.

Property registration windows follow the Bhumi kraya verses of the Vastu chapter, daytime only, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, in the soft and fixed nakshatras, on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

New venture and launch windows use the same Vyapara table as a business start, daytime only, on tithis 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, in the soft and fixed nakshatras, on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Education start (Vidyarambha) windows follow the Samskara chapter, daytime only, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 11 and 12 and their Krishna counterparts, in the nakshatras it names for learning (Ashwini, Mrigashira, Ardra, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Revati), on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.

Windows for a planned, non-emergency medical procedure follow the Aushadha and Shastra-karma verses, daytime only, on tithis 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11 and 13 and their Krishna counterparts, in the nakshatras they name (Ashwini, Mrigashira, Punarvasu, Pushya, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Anuradha, Uttara Ashadha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Uttara Bhadrapada, Revati), on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, and never replace the doctor's schedule.

Vrat start windows follow the Dharmasindhu and the Vrata-arambha verses, daytime only, on tithis 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 13 and Purnima and their Krishna counterparts, in the soft and fixed nakshatras, on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday or Friday.
The classical nama-akshara table assigns one starting syllable to each of the 108 nakshatra padas, and the Moon's nakshatra pada at birth gives the syllable a name traditionally begins with.

Varna koota (1 point) compares the varna class of the two Moon signs (Brahmin for Karka, Vrishchika and Meena, Kshatriya for Mesha, Simha and Dhanu, Vaishya for Vrishabha, Kanya and Makara, Shudra for Mithuna, Tula and Kumbha) and gives the point when the first side's class is the same or higher.

Vashya koota (2 points) compares the vashya class of the two Moon signs (Chatushpada, Manava, Jalachara, Vanachara, Keeta, with Dhanu and Makara split by half-sign) and scores 2 for the same class, 1 or ½ for friendly classes and 0 for hostile ones.
Tara koota (3 points) counts each Moon nakshatra from the other and divides by nine, giving 1½ points for each direction whose remainder is not 3, 5 or 7 (Vipat, Pratyari, Vadha).
Yoni koota (4 points) compares the animal class of the two birth nakshatras, scoring 4 for the same animal, 2 for neutral pairs, 1 for unfriendly pairs and 0 for the sworn-enemy pairs of the table.

Graha Maitri koota (5 points) compares the lords of the two Moon signs by Parashara's natural friendships, scoring 5 for the same lord or mutual friends, 4 for friend and neutral, 3 for both neutral, 1 for friend and enemy, ½ for neutral and enemy and 0 for mutual enemies.

Gana koota (6 points) compares the gana (Deva, Manushya, Rakshasa) of the two birth nakshatras, scoring 6 for the same gana, 5 for Deva with Manushya, 1 for Manushya with Rakshasa and 0 for Deva with Rakshasa.

Bhakoot koota (7 points) counts the sign distance between the two Moons and gives all 7 points unless the pair is 2/12, 5/9 or 6/8 apart (Bhakoot dosha) or both Moons share one nakshatra pada, in which cases it gives 0.
Nadi koota (8 points) compares the nadi (Adi, Madhya, Antya) of the two birth nakshatras and gives all 8 points for different nadis and 0 for the same nadi (Nadi dosha) unless an exception lifts it.
Nadi dosha is lifted, and the full 8 points given, when both Moons are in the same sign but in different nakshatras.
Nadi dosha is lifted, and the full 8 points given, when both Moons are in the same nakshatra but in different padas, while the same nakshatra and the same pada keeps the dosha.

The traditional exception that lifts Bhakoot dosha when both Moon signs have the same lord (Mesha–Vrishchika, Vrishabha–Tula, Mithuna–Kanya, Dhanu–Meena, Makara–Kumbha) is named on the row but not scored, so the total matches Drik Panchang's convention.
Bhakoot scores 0 when both Moons share the same nakshatra and the same pada, even though the sign distance itself is fine (eka-nakshatra eka-pada convention).

Mangal dosha is present when Mars stands in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th house counted from the Lagna, from the Moon or from Venus, and it is called effective only when none of the listed cancellation rules applies (the Lagna reference is skipped when the birth time is unknown).
Mangal dosha is cancelled when Mars stands in its own sign (Mesha or Vrishchika) or in its exaltation sign (Makara).
Mangal dosha is cancelled when Mars stands in Mesha in the 1st house, in Vrishchika in the 4th, in Makara in the 7th, in Karka in the 8th or in Dhanu in the 12th.
Mangal dosha is cancelled when Mars shares its sign with Jupiter or with the Moon.
Mangal dosha is cancelled when Jupiter aspects Mars, that is when Mars stands in the 5th, 7th or 9th sign from Jupiter.
Mangal dosha is cancelled when Mars is debilitated (in Karka) or combust, since a weakened Mars is held unable to produce the dosha.
Mangal dosha is balanced when both charts carry an effective dosha, the classical mutual cancellation between two Manglik horoscopes.

The 7th-house lords of the two charts are compared by Parashara's natural friendships and reported as harmonious (same planet or friends), mixed (neutral) or challenging (enemies), marked approx. when a birth time is unknown.

The two Venus placements are compared by sign distance, harmonious at 1/7, 3/11 and 5/9, mixed at 4/10 and challenging at 2/12 and 6/8, with each Venus's dignity and the relation of the sign lords listed.
The two Moon signs are compared by sign distance, harmonious at 1/7, 3/11 and 5/9, mixed at 4/10 and challenging at 2/12 and 6/8, downgraded to mixed when the sign lords are natural enemies.

The two Vimshottari trees over the next five years are laid side by side at antardasha level and each overlap is labelled by the natural relationship of the two mahadasha lords, the row reading harmonious when friendly overlaps cover more than half the time, challenging when hostile ones do, and mixed otherwise.

The avakahada chakra lists the birth classifications a Janam Patri prints, varna, vashya, yoni, gana and nadi from the Moon's sign and nakshatra, the nakshatra with its charan (pada) and lord, the rashi (Moon sign), the Lagna, the element of the Moon sign and the name syllable, all from the same tables the matching kootas use.

The ghatak chakra lists, for the birth Moon sign, the lunar month (Purnimanta name), tithi group, weekday, nakshatra, yoga, karana, Moon sign and Lagna that the classical table marks as unfavourable for that native's important beginnings.

Every report states the ayanamsa and its value, the node method (mean or true), the ephemeris, the time-zone table release, the house system, the rounding applied and the rule ids of the conventions it used, so each printed value can be traced.

A Prashna chart is cast for the instant the question is asked, at the place where it is asked, with the same ayanamsa and node settings as a birth chart, and is read for that question rather than for the asker's life as a whole.
In a Prashna the rising sign of the hour stands for the asker and its lord for the matter asked about, so the reading begins from the Lagna of the moment and the planetary hora running at that time.
The question text, the time and the place of a Prashna are stored only in this phone's database and are never sent anywhere; deleting the entry removes them.

Explain only from the computed chart you are given, naming the planet, sign, house, nakshatra or dasha the explanation rests on, and say plainly when the chart does not contain what the question needs.
Every claim must cite the id of a rule from the supplied corpus snippets, and claims with no rule to cite are left out rather than invented.

Never promise, predict or date an outcome, never use fear or urgency, never attach a percentage or a score of correctness, and describe what the tradition reads a placement for rather than what will happen.

Give no medical, legal or financial advice of any kind and recommend no gemstone, puja, product, service or person; when a question asks for such advice, say that this is outside what the chart can answer.
Use the supplied corpus snippets in the reader's language as the only source of interpretive wording, so that the answer says what the Why? sheets of this app say and nothing the corpus does not.

The model runs on this phone without a network, can misread the chart or the rules, and must answer briefly in plain language, in the reader's register, without claiming to be an astrologer or a person.

Every answer from the on-device model is shown under the fixed line AI explanation from your chart, can be wrong, followed by the rule ids it used, because a language model can be fluent and mistaken at the same time.
